column2: The best teacher should contemplate at the navel a strong triad; and a twelve-petalled lotus he should contemplate in the middle of the lotus.
In its middle, having meditated on the Person's power and worshipped, the teacher, having placed Hari in the image, should worship the gods there.
With scent, flowers and the rest properly, with limbs and enclosure, in order; with the twelve-syllable seeds one should worship Keshava and the others.
In the twelve-spoked mandala the guardians of the world and the rest in order; afterward the twice-born should worship the image with scent, flowers and the rest.
With the Purusha-sukta and the Shri-sukta, the pedestal; afterward, in order beginning with the producing, one should kindle the Vaishnava fire.
Having offered, "Agni is offered" — the wise one should lead the fire into the pit. The mantra in leading the fire: "You, Agni, are called Agni."
In the south, "Agni is offered" — the wise one should lead the fire into the pit. "Agnim agnim" in the east; the wise one should lead the fire into the pit.
In the north one should lead the fire: "We call Agni, Agni." The mantra in leading the fire: "You, Agni, are called Agni."
One thousand and eight sticks of palasha, in each pit one should offer rice grains with the Vedas and the rest likewise;
sesame with ghee, with the utterances, with the root-mantra; one should make ghee; then the peace-offering with the three sweets.
With the twelve-syllable mantra one should touch the feet, navel, heart and head; having offered ghee, curds and milk, one should touch the head and then
having touched head, navel and feet, one should set up four rivers: Ganga, Yamuna, Goda, and Sarasvati by name in order.
One should burn with the Vishnu-gayatri, cook the porridge with the Gayatri, offer, give the offering, and in the north feed the Brahmins.

To satisfy the lords of the Saman he should give a golden cow to the teacher. Having given offerings to the guardians of the quarters, one should keep vigil at night, with the sound of Brahma-songs and the like, by dwelling on all shares.
To the Person who has passed beyond the qualities, the great-souled, the imperishable, the ancient, Vishnu, be present.
Whatever is your supreme principle and whatever is your body made of knowledge — let all that be awakened together in this body.
Having made oneself present, with Brahma and the other attendants, with his own name one should place the others, the weapons, with the proper mudra.
Seeing the procession, year and the like, Hari is to be known as present; having bowed, praised with hymns, and recited the eight-syllable and the rest,
the teacher should go out and worship the door-guards Chanda and Prachanda; having approached the fire pavilion, one should set up and worship Garuda.
Having established and worshipped the lords of the quarters and gods in their directions, the teacher having established Vishvaksena should worship the conch, discus and the rest.
One should offer an offering to all attendants and to the elements; one should give the teacher a fee of supreme garments, gold and the like.
The man should present to the teacher the materials useful for the sacrifice; half the teacher's fee he should give to the priests.
He should give fees to others, then feed the Brahmins. The teacher should give unrestricted fruits to the sacrificer.
The installer leads Vishnu and his whole family by himself. This is the common rule for all gods; their root-mantras differ; the rest to be done alike.
Having soaked with mercury, one should cover with an eye-band. Then one should place the wheel and recall Narahari in its middle.
Om Kshraum, homage to Narasimha — one should worship and establish Hari. Then the sacrificer with his kin, taking the banner,
should place the tip of the banner in a vessel with curds and rice; one should worship the banner with the first mantra ending in "phat."
Having placed that vessel on the head, remembering Narayana, one should circumambulate with the sound of the fourth auspicious instruments.
Then one should place the staff with the eight-syllable mantra; the wise one should release the banner with the hymn "I release you."
The Brahmin should give the vessel, banner, elephant and the rest to the teacher. This is declared the common rule in raising a banner.
Whatever mark belongs to a god, he should keep firm with its mantra. By the gift of a banner one goes to heaven and the king becomes mighty.
Having shown a book in a mirror, one should sprinkle with pots as before. Having done the opening of the eyes, the man should place it on a couch.
One should place the Purusha-sukta and the god-first hymn on that book; having made it living, having worshipped and offered porridge,
having eaten, one should feed the Brahmins, teachers and the rest with fees. The book should be carried by men on a chariot or an elephant.
In a house or temple and so on, having set up the book one should worship it; wrapped in cloth and the rest, one should worship it at the beginning and end of recital.
Having determined world-peace, the man should have the book read. One chapter, he should sprinkle the sacrificer and others from the pot.
Having given a book to a Brahmin, there is no end to the fruit. They say three are the supreme gifts: cows, earth and learning.
Having given the fruit of the gift of knowledge, the heap of leaves up to the ink — as many as the number of leaves and letters, sinless one,
so many thousands of years he is honored in Vishnu's world. The man who gives the Pancharatra, Puranas and Mahabharata, having lifted up twenty-one families, is absorbed in the supreme truth.
When the portion is divided by seven, one learned in Garga's knowledge, divided in eight, the remainder is the expense gone.
Or the wise one should multiply the cubit-figure by seven; when divided by eight, one should arrange earth and the rest.
Banner, smoke, lion, dog, bull, ass, elephant, and crow — these arise in the east and the rest; one should consider.
A three-halled triple is praised, excluding the north and east; with a neighbor's house in the south, a two-halled one is always obtained.
In the south, one-hall or west-hall; two one-halls are praised; the others are fearful.
A four-halled one is always praised, free of all faults. One should make a house of one storey and so on up to seven storeys.
Without door, altar and the rest, free of filling; a god's house by the rule of consecration of the deity always.
Having established and by the rite stated for the community of men, in the morning having done a bath with all herbs, pure and unwearied,
having fed Brahmins with sweets, adorned with full pots and the like, with an arch, having had "svasti" pronounced, with the cow-pen...
the householder should enter the house, having honored astrologers; in the house he should recite this nourishing mantra, composed:

Om, Nanda, gladden, Vasishthi, with the Vasus and offspring; Jaya, descendant of Bhrigu, bringer of victory to creatures;
agnipuran:65:18	Purna, descendant of Angiras, make me fulfilled; Bhadra, descendant of Kashyapa, make my mind auspicious;
agnipuran:65:19	endowed with all seeds and herbs, covered with all jewels and herbs, lovely Nandana, Nanda, Vasishthi, delight here.
agnipuran:65:20	Daughter of Prajapati, goddess, four-sided, greatest, fortunate, of good vows, goddess, Kashyapi, delight in the house.
agnipuran:65:21	Worshipped by the supreme teachers, adorned with scent and garlands, bringer of prosperity, goddess, Bhargavi, delight in the house.
agnipuran:65:22	Unmanifest, manifest, full, daughter of the sage Angiras, brick, grant the desired; I have the consecration made.
agnipuran:65:23	In the possession of the lord of the region, lord of the town and lord of the house, increase men, wealth, elephants, horses and cattle.
Having shown a mirror, lamp-waving, with songs and instruments auspicious, one should worship with a fan, worship, lamp, scent, flowers and the rest.
Turmeric, mung, saffron, white powder and the like on the head of the image; for the devotees, held, gives the fruit of all pilgrim places.
Having bathed and worshipped, the procession image set on the chariot — the teacher should lead it with the sounds of the rivers, with umbrellas and the rest and the guardians of the land.
Within a yojana of the river one should have an altar made there; having taken him down from the vehicle, one should set him on that altar.
There one should cook porridge and offer the pudding; then with Vedic mantras on the waters one should invoke the holy places.
With the "Apo hi shtha" and Upanishadic hymns one should worship with arghya chiefly; again, taking the god, in the water doing the Aghamarshana,

one should bathe with the great ones and Brahmins; having brought him out one should place him on the altar. Having worshipped that day, one should lead him to the temple; the teacher should worship at the fire; it gives enjoyment and liberation.
Sahadevi, Kumari, Simhi, Vyaghri, Amrita, Vishnuparni, Shatashiva, Vacha — one should place divine herbs.
In the east and others, in the nine of the north, in the middle one should place a pot of curds. Leaf, cardamom, bark, kushtha, balaka, two sandals,
creeper, musk and black agaru in order; the perfected materials in the east and others; peace-water together;
camphor, in order, white, mountain-essence, tin one should place; the essence of cloud and head, and jewels in the east and others.
Having anointed with ghee and rubbed, one should bathe with the root-mantra; one should worship with scent and the rest, offer in fire and give the full oblation.
One should give the offering to all beings and feed, having given fees. Having established the god with gods, sages and kings, the lords
became so; having established thus one should perform the bathing festival; by a thousand and eight pots he becomes share-taker in all.
By the concluding bath of the sacrifice, the full bathing is done. The marriage of Gauri and Lakshmi and festivals are preceded by bathing.
Then the indwelling of Indra and others and the oblation of the lord of the forest should be done; from the middle of the tree one should release a cow; then by the anointing mantra,
with Rik, Yajus and Saman mantras and with Varuna mantras, auspicious sounds, and tree-altar pots, the bathing, best of Brahmins,
of the trees and of the sacrificer the sacrificers should do. Adorned, he should give a fee of cow, land, ornaments and clothes.
He should give food with milk for four days. The oblation should be done with sesame and the rest and with palasha sticks.
